To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EMA has demonstrated successful operation with the high-rate lithium ion batteries and cross-platform controller.

the EMA and controller were successfully integrated and demonstrated in a developmental test bed, the EMA was able to achieve 100% of its rated thrust and torque requirements, the EMA and common controller were able to meet the required control performance and stability requirements, and the common controller was successfully integrated across dissimilar launch platforms.
the EMA and the common controller are capable of meeting the performance requirements and that the EMA is a viable alternative to hydraulic thrust vector control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of ETVC systems and the integration of ETVC systems with a common controller architecture.
the development of an electric actuator and control system that is compatible with multiple launch vehicle platforms.
the development of ETVC technology and its application to the next generation launch vehicles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ETVC system has demonstrated the ability to provide thrust vector control in a manner similar to the current hydrazine based system with the added benefit of reduced recurring costs.
the developmental EMA and controller have demonstrated the ability to provide thrust vector control to a 100,000 lbf liquid oxygen and liquid hydrogen engine.

the ETVC technology has been demonstrated to be viable for manned launch vehicle applications and that the technology has been successfully integrated and tested on a cross platform common controller architecture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the EMA and the cross platform extensibility of the controller architecture can be used to reduce launch vehicle complexity, reduce recurring launch costs, reduce development costs and increase launch vehicle performance.
the ETVC systems are viable and ready for flight qualification testing.
the ETVC systems are viable for future manned launch vehicles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ETVC systems can be developed and qualified to meet the demanding requirements of launch vehicle flight applications.
the EMA and common controller are capable of meeting or exceeding performance specifications for a manned launch vehicle.
a common controller architecture can be developed that will support a wide range of electric thrusters across a variety of platforms.
